headline: A softer US PPI steadies Wall Street, but the rate-hike story stands
tone: The 14:30 data took the edge off the rate scare without resetting the day: US stocks opened higher, Europe slipped back to flat and the oil bid returned.
body: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% forecast, with core in line at 0.3%. The annual rate still climbed to 6.5%, the highest since November 2022, and markets keep a December Fed hike fully priced.

Wall Street opened higher: the S&P 500 is up 0.3% at 7,613, the Dow up 0.3% and the Nasdaq up 0.1%, with Nvidia bouncing modestly after this week's sell-off. Europe gave back its midday gain: the STOXX 600 is down 0.1% at 663.15, the DAX down 0.1% and the SMI down 0.5%.
Oil is bid again: Brent is up 1.1% at $96.86 and WTI up 0.7% at $89.38, after Brent sat flat near $95.75 at midday. US gas fell 3.3% to $3.23, while TTF is little changed at €92.56.
The dollar stays firm: EUR/USD is down 0.4% at 1.105 and USD/CHF up 0.7% at 0.838. The US 5-year is at 4.97% and the 30-year at 5.48%; our 10-year feed still shows Thursday's 5.10% close, up 12bp.

views.text: Still into oil and out of renewables. Equinor is up 1.9%, Shell 1.7%, TotalEnergies 1.6% and BP 1.3%, and the XLE energy ETF is up 0.8%. Acciona Energía is down 6.4%, Grenergy 4.5%, Eolus 4.5% and Orrön 4.6%. Copper is down 0.9% and silver 1.2%, with gold flat at $3,886.

The live gauge reads +4, which is mixed. The S&P 500 3.7% above its 200-day average, the STOXX 600 5.3% above, and a VIX down 4% to 18.0 pull toward risk on. Thursday's 12bp jump in the US 10-year, a firmer dollar and copper lagging gold by 0.9% pull the other way; only 8 of 14 indices are up.

views.section: What to watch into the close
views.text: Whether the US gains hold into the weekend and yields stay contained after the PPI. Next week's big test is Nvidia's results on Tuesday.
